question: I have only Basic Autoplan and caused a crash in B.C. What coverage distinction matters before I assume my own car's repairs will be paid?
generated_answer: You have a Basic Autoplan policy, which provides basic third-party liability coverage and some protection for you in case you are injured in an accident. However, this policy does not cover damages to your own vehicle. The key distinction in your case is that you were involved in an accident in British Columbia, which has a no-fault insurance system. This means that your own insurance company will cover the damages to your vehicle, regardless of who was at fault in the accident. You should contact your insurance company to file a claim and obtain a detailed explanation of your coverage and the process for submitting a claim.
